sections.title: CORE Safety Rules
sections.text:
Train & Engine Safety Rule Book - CPKC 
April 2023
Organizing the Information
The Train & Engine Safety Rule Book is organized into two main sections:
Section I:
Core Safety Rules: These are common rules to all functions and must be complied with 
and enforced at all times. 
Section II:
Safety Rules: These are function specific rules that must be complied with and enforced 
at all times. They are written to address the work of Train & Engine employees. 
Safe Work Procedures: These procedures outline the steps to safely perform the task. 
Safe work procedures must be complied with at all times. 
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) Chart: This chart has been created to assist 
the user in determining the appropriate PPE that is required based on the task to 
be performed. 
4

April 2023 
Train & Engine Safety Rule Book - CPKC
CORE Safety Rules
1. Rights and Responsibilities
All employees must make certain that:
	
• Job tasks are performed only by individuals who are qualified and authorized. 
	
• Job briefings/task assessments are conducted before performing work and when 
activity and/or conditions change. 
	
• We advise and redirect to safe work practices anyone observed performing an 
unsafe act. 
	
• We immediately inform each other of unsafe conditions, correct/protect it and 
report it to a supervisor. 
	
• Accidents, incidents, including injuries, and related information are immediately 
reported to a supervisor. 
	
• Warning signs, posted instructions, placards, and/or barriers marking restricted 
areas and lockout tagout areas are displayed and complied with at all times. 
	
• We do not participate in horseplay or physical altercations while on Company 
property or participating in Company activities. 
	
• One person does not engage in work activity that by legislation or Company 
policy requires two or more people. 
	
• A copy of the function specific safety rules must be accessible while on duty. 
	
• We do not possess or use a firearm on Company property unless authorized by 
CPKC Police Services. 
2. Substance Abuse
	
• Inappropriate substance use is prohibited as identified in CPKC Drug & 
Alcohol Policies. 
	
• Do not smoke/use electronic cigarettes in company buildings, vehicles, 
and machines.
	
• For more information see CPKC HR Policy. 
3. Non-CPKC Personnel 
Employees responsible for non-CPKC personnel must:
	
• Understand the terms of the Minimum Safety Requirements for Contractors 
working on CPKC property, follow access control procedures, and ensure they; 
o  Receive a site-specific safety orientation and job briefing.
o  Wear PPE according to location-specific requirements. 
o  Do not foul track without proper protection.
o  Have a Contractor Site Safety Plan/Emergency Information Sheet. 
o  Have appropriate identification. 
4. Emergencies and Derailments
	
• Follow all notification procedures as outlined in location-specific Emergency 
Response Plans. 
	
• Approach an emergency or a derailment site only when safe to do so. 
5

Train & Engine Safety Rule Book - CPKC 
April 2023
	
• When arriving at an emergency site, contact the On-Scene Response Coordinator 
or Person-In-Charge for a job briefing and follow all procedures outlined in the 
job briefing. 
	
• Following an accident or incident, immediately notify a supervisor/dispatcher and 
do not contact human remains, blood, or other fluids.
5. Fire Safety
	
• Maintain unrestricted access to, and be familiar with the location of, fire 
extinguishers, alarm boxes, exit aisles, circuit breakers, fuse panels, emergency 
exits and local emergency response plans.
	
• Immediately replace or report any defective, discharged or missing fire 
extinguishers. 
	
• Store flammable and combustible material away from ignition sources.
	
• When qualified, use proper grounding and bonding techniques to prevent static 
electrical charge when dispensing or transferring flammable liquids. 
	
• Do not leave open flames unattended. 
	
• Dispose of flammable or combustible materials according to established 
Company guidelines.
	
• Upon discovery of a fire, if safe to do so, extinguish the fire. Employees must 
immediately activate the fire alarm (where available), and promptly report the 
fire to supervisor, dispatcher and/or proper authority.
6. Work Environment
	
• Keep all work areas clean, orderly, and free from clutter and debris. 
	
• Must properly dispose of refuse in appropriate and approved receptacle or 
waste bin. 
	
• Employees who use needles, lancets and medical sharps must properly dispose of 
them in sharps containers, if provided, or remove them from company property 
for disposal, if not provided.  Do not throw needles, lancets, and medical sharps 
in company trash.
	
• Use approved products to wash equipment, clothing, or floors. 
	
• Do not use compressed air or gases to remove debris from body or clothing. 
	
• Do not walk under suspended loads. 
	
• Work materials must be kept neatly and not stored above shoulder height unless 
the area is designed for palletized equipment/materials with a specified load 
limit and a forklift is utilized.
	
• Walkways must be kept clear to eliminate tripping hazards. 
7. Vehicles, Materials, Equipment, and Tools
	
• Operate, maintain, and repair vehicles, equipment, tools, and materials only 
when qualified, properly licensed and authorized. 
	
• Use CSA B376 or equivalent UL / ULC (CAN) or Department of Transportation 
(DOT) (US/Mexico) approved, properly marked containers when storing or 
transporting flammable liquids or materials.
	
• Use approved tools, equipment, and materials for the purpose(s) intended. 
	
• Do not modify or override safety devices or remove safety guards. 
6

sections.title: Train & Engine Safety Rules and Safe Work Procedures
sections.text:
April 2023 
Train & Engine Safety Rule Book - CPKC
	
• Maintain, repair, and store equipment according to prescribed instructions. 
	
• Inspect all vehicles, equipment, tools, and related safety devices for unsafe 
conditions before use. 
	
• Repair or tag and remove from service if defective. 
	
• Use three-point contact when getting on or off any equipment, machinery, 
ladder, or vehicle. 
	
• Face the vehicle or equipment/track unit when getting on or off. 
	
• Ventilate exhaust when operating internal-combustion equipment inside 
buildings or enclosed structures. 
8. Office Safety
	
• When sitting in a chair, keep all chair legs or casters on the floor. 
	
• When not in use, chairs shall be kept pushed in to keep walkways and 
workspaces clear. 
	
• Roller style chairs are only allowed at workstations, training, and 
meeting/office rooms. 
	
• Fixed leg chairs are required at ready room and lunch tables. 
	
• Use only commercially available stepstools that meet CSA standards (CAN)/ANSI 
Standards (US/Mexico) to access elevated locations.
	
• Ensure that desk and file cabinet doors and drawers are closed when not in use. 
	
• When ascending or descending flights of stairs employees must utilize handrails. 
9. Use of Electronic Devices
For Employees governed by GCOR/OTS or CROR refer to the applicable operating rules 
and related system special instructions. 
For employees not governed by GCOR/OTS or CROR refer to the CPKC Use of Electronic 
Devices Procedure for applicable instructions.

Ensure 3-point protection is in place. 
Step 2: 	
Close both angle cocks. 
Step 3: 	
Crouching down, firmly grasp each glad hand with your hand near the coupling. 
Step 4: 	
With your arm extended and with a quick motion, pull upward on the

T-4 Vehicles Used for Company Business
1.	
Inspect vehicles for unsafe conditions before use. Repair or tag and remove from 
service if defective. 
2.	
Prior to operation of a vehicle the driver must conduct a walk around of the 
vehicle to identify any obstacles, clearance restrictions, or adjacent vehicles that 
may interfere with executing a safe movement. When backing up use a spotter 
if one is readily available.
3.	
Headlights/daytime running lights must be on when operating a vehicle.
4.	
Wear seat belt while operating or riding in motor vehicles equipped with 
them, unless engaged in inspections and traveling less than 15 MPH (25 KPH) 
on CPKC property.
5.	
While being transported in vehicles, ride only in seats permanently installed or 
in approved, identified riding locations. 
6.	
Do not use hand held cell phones while operating a company vehicle or mobile 
equipment while it is in motion on any type of road except in an emergency. 
7.	
Use company provided cell phones, hands free only, for limited use while 
operating a company vehicle or mobile equipment if: 
	
• It is solely for company business; 
	
• It is safe to do so; and 
	
• The vehicle or mobile equipment being operated is NOT on a public roadway 
in a province, state, or other jurisdiction where such use is in violation of any 
law or regulation. 
8.	
Do not get on or off a moving vehicle. 
9.	
While transporting tools, materials and equipment with a company vehicle on 
road or track, loads must be contained, immobilized or secured. 
10.	 Do not park foul of the track, unless track protection is provided and only 
when necessary.

sections.text:
April 2023 
Train & Engine Safety Rule Book - CPKC
T-5 Aligning Drawbar / Coupler
1.	
Separate equipment by a minimum of 50 feet. 
2.	
Ensure that equipment is secured and 3-point protection is provided. 
3.	
Do not adjust coupler by kicking it with your foot. 
4.	
Do not lift a drawbar. 
Safe Work Procedure: Aligning Coupler with Backwards or Forward 
Facing Method 
Step 1:	
Ensure three point protection is in place and/or cars 
are secured with a minimum of 50 feet separation.
Step 2:	
Stand to the side of the coupler.
Step 3:	
Face or turn your back to the coupler leaning 
against it.
Step 4:	
Put one foot beneath the coupler, one foot in front 
of you or one foot behind you, depending on the 
method.
Step 5:	
Watch your footing, especially during wet and/or 
winter conditions. Do not step on the rail when 
walking; however, it is permitted to brace your 
foot on the rail for added leverage when aligning 
the drawbar using this technique.
Step 6:	
Grip the coupler from beneath and watch your 
fingers.
Step 7:	
Keep the load close to your body.
Step 8:	
Bend at the knees and hips while maintaining a 
neutral spine.
Step 9:	
Raise up from the knees, using your leg muscles, 
and shift your weight forwards or backwards to 
push the drawbar over. Do not lift the drawbar or elevate your shoulders 
when pushing.
Step 10:	 Use whole body movements, pushing small distances, stopping and 
repositioning as needed (repeating the steps above) until the drawbar is 
aligned. Do not over exert.
T-6 Coupling / Uncoupling
1.	
Before coupling cars:
	
• If riding equipment prior to coupling, detrain (if riding a locomotive, you are 
exempt from detraining); and 
	
• Ensure couplers are aligned and that at least one knuckle is open. 
2.	
Only use an operating lever under the following conditions:
	
• while stopped 
	
• at a walking pace facing the direction of travel, never run; or

T-14 Hand Brakes
1.	
Fully release all hand brakes prior to moving 
equipment, unless cabling a car or applying 
GCOR 7.12. 
2.	
When operating wheel-type hand brakes, always 
grip the brake wheel with your thumb on the 
outside of the wheel rim and never overexert. 
3.	
Do not apply or release wheel style hand brakes 
from the ground unless the bottom of the 
handbrake wheel is at shoulder height or below. 
4.	
When releasing hand brakes check at least 
two cars beyond the last hand brake found to 
ensure there are no more hand brakes applied. 
5.	
It is permissible to apply a hand brake for the purpose of controlling free rolling 
equipment, the handbrake must only be applied with sufficient force not to cause 
the wheels to slide or lock up. 
6.	
Never use both hands or a foot to operate a hand brake. Exception: Both 
hands may be used to operate a staff-type brake and a foot may be used to 
operate the pawl.
7.	
Where authorized by SVP Operations, Company approved brake sticks may be 
used to operate vertical wheel style hand brakes, retainer valves, open knuckles, 
angle cocks and press the reset button on an EOT on stationary equipment. The 
use of defective brake sticks is prohibited. 
When using a brake stick to operate a handbrake:
	
• If practicable, work from the Field side rather than between adjacent tracks. 
	
• If working between adjacent tracks keep clear of moving equipment. 
	
• Crew members must comply with the requirements of T-27 3-point protection. 
	
• Place the hook to the outside of the wheel to avoid the hook from being 
caught between the wheel and the equipment. 
	
• Never place the butt of the brake stick against your body, keep it at the side 
of your body. 
	
• Never cross equipment with the brake stick in hand, pass it through 
equipment 
	
• Never walk backwards 
	
• Do not place the brake stick: 
o  on or remove from moving equipment 
o  in a location where it may be an obstruction or tripping hazard 
	
• Do not use the brake stick to:
o  Operate defective hand brake wheels
o  Operate quick release handles
8.	
Keep your body and hands free of all moving parts eg. chain, wheel, release 
handle. 
9.	
Never use hand brake wheel as a handhold.
16

T-19 On or About Locomotives
1.	
Use door handles or other opening/closing devices to open /close doors or 
windows whenever provided. 
2.	
Keep locomotive cab and walkways clean, free of debris, clutter and slip/trip 
hazards. 
3.	
Ask for assistance when placing grips, bags, MU cables, tools, EOT’s etc. on 
locomotives, if required. 
4.	
When running the units through flange ways that may be obstructed with 
snow, ice or other material. You should detrain and walk clear of the movement 
watching for wheel climb until you are beyond the condition. 
5.	
Store tools, EOT’s and MU cables in the designated locations.
T-20 On or About Tracks
1.	
Do not sit or lean against rail equipment. 
2.	
Look in both directions before:
	
• Fouling or crossing any track 
	
• Getting on or off equipment; or 
	
• Operating a switch. 
3.	
Never walk or stand foul of a track between the rails or on the shoulder tie 
ends, unless there are no other viable options available and it is safe to do so. 
4.	
When walking between standing equipment, ensure there is a minimum of 50 
feet of separation between equipment. 
5.	
Allow at least 15 feet when passing around the end of standing equipment 
unless proper protection is provided. 
6.	
Maintain a safe distance from moving equipment to avoid protruding objects. 
7.	
Do not step on any part of: 
	
• a rail; 
	
• a switch or switch machine/ heater except to operate foot pedal; 
	
• a frog; 
	
• a derail; 
	
• a retarder; 
	
• a defect detector/hot box detector; 
	
• Automatic Equipment Identification (AEI) reader; or 
	
• Wayside interface unit (WIU). 
8.	
At night and during periods of reduced visibility, use a lantern or approved light 
source to perform work. 
	
• All T&E employees MUST use a CPKC supplied hand lantern as an approved 
light source to perform work. 
	
• It is permissible for all T&E employees to use a headlamp in addition to the 
CPKC supplied hand held lantern to perform work.

9.	
Lanterns must always be carried by hand or through your arm and never clipped 
to your body. 
Exception:
	
• Locomotive engineers may use a hand held flashlight while performing the 
duties of a locomotive engineer. 
10.	 When traversing a bridge be aware of weather conditions, lighting conditions 
and bridge surface conditions. Walk between the rails if no walkway is provided. 
11.	 If found in a situation where you are located between adjacent track 
movements, kneel down and stop the movement you are controlling. 
12.	 When working at or near crossings, train crews must avoid using hand signals 
for train operations, which could be misunderstood by motorists using the 
crossing. 
13.	 Before going between or working on the end of rail equipment that does not 
have a locomotive coupled to it: 
	
• a crew member, must verbally inform other crew members, and other crews 
working in close proximity by radio and receive acknowledgment from those 
notified. 
	
• must not be coupled to and/or handbrakes released that could affect the 
movement of such equipment without permission from the crew member 
that is between or at the end of rail equipment. 
14.	 When duties require you to cross a track, walk directly across the track at a right 
angle (90-degrees). Employees must look both ways prior to each track and 
apply a 90-Degree principle when conditions permit.

When walking ahead of a movement, ensure you check the position of the movement 
often and never foul the track.

April 2023 
Train & Engine Safety Rule Book - CPKC
T-24 Riding Equipment
1.	
Use the side ladder of the lead end of equipment 
on the engineers side whenever possible and 
always observe the direction of travel. Whenever 
possible ride on the engineers side. 
2.	
It is permissible to ride the platform of a 
locomotive, or other equipment with a designated 
riding platform (e.g. passenger cars).
3.	
It is permissible to ride the platform of the leading 
end of a tank car with the employees feet outside of 
the rail and body positioned outside of the handrail.
4.	
It is permissible to ride the end platform of a car 
only on the trailing end of a movement.
5.	
It is prohibited to move from one car to another car while moving. (unless 
equipment is designed for movement between cars i.e. locomotives, passenger 
cars, rail grinding train, etc.)
6.	
Always maintain at least 3 points of contact using foot, crook of arm or hands. 
When riding equipment, use only designated handholds and ensure your feet 
are facing the stirrup, ladder or stairwell, prepared for slack action.
7.	
The following is prohibited, do not ride:
	
• the lead end platform or front ladder of equipment except as noted in 
#3 above or when operating a handbrake on cars rolling under their own 
momentum;
	
• on the deck of a flat car, bulkhead or centerbeam;
	
• a flat car not equipped with handholds extending at least 18 inches above 
the deck of the car;
	
• middle ladder on a tank car;
	
• on any equipment while entering, inside, or leaving any building or structure;
	
• on the roof of any rolling stock or on the lading of any car;
	
• inside the end cage of equipment;
	
• inside a gondola; or
	
• between cars unless operating a handbrake on cars rolling under their own 
momentum.
8.	
It is prohibited to ride the bottom step of equipment over public crossings at grade.
9.	
When conditions permit ride on the opposite side of an adjacent track where 
equipment is present.
10.	 Ride the side ladder of equipment, only if hand holds and stirrup configuration 
allow for a firm grip and an erect and normal body position. Never lean your 
upper body back from the side ladder unless it is safe to do so. Ensure there are 
no switch stands, equipment in adjacent tracks, or other clearance issues. 
11.	 Always advise the locomotive engineer or controlling operator that you are 
riding equipment.

sections.title: T-27 3-Point Protection
sections.text:
Train & Engine Safety Rule Book - CPKC 
April 2023
T-26 Switches
1.	
Keep your body, hands, and feet clear of all moving parts and out of the path of 
the switch handle. 
2.	
Do not apply force with your foot on a switch/derail handle. 
3.	
Prior to operating switches, check the switch rods and switch points for ice, 
ballast, or any other debris that may prevent the switch from lining freely. Check 
if the switch has been spiked. 
4.	
Remove the switch point lock pedal, where equipped, before operating switch. 
5.	
Ensure switch points fit properly prior to allowing a movement to pass. 
6.	
Reapply the switch lock or keeper after the switch has been lined. 
7.	
Never use excessive force while operating a switch. 
8.	
Use both hands while operating the switch handle to align the switch points 
or derail.
Safe Work Procedure: Cleaning Switches - Winter Months
Step 1:	
Using switch broom, clean area between the switch points and the heel blocks.
Step 2:	
When cleaning the switch points, ensure that they are free of ice and hard-
packed snow. (The switch points glide on the switch plates.) 
Step 3:	
Start with a wide stance to create a stable base of support. Position your 
feet so your hips and shoulders face the work to minimize twisting and side 
bending. Bend at the hips and knees, with your back in neutral while you 
sweep the brush across your body. Use short strokes and move your feet to 
avoid twisting or overreaching.
Step 4:	
To pick at any ice, use the scraper tool on the opposite end of the handle and 
bend deeper through the hips and knees to get close to the work (without 
bending through the back). 
Step 5:	
Clean connecting rods.
Step 6:	
Ensure switch points are thoroughly and properly cleaned and there is no 
gap between the switch point and stock rail.

sections.title: Service (RCLS / RCO)
sections.text:
April 2023 
Train & Engine Safety Rule Book - CPKC
T-27 3-Point Protection
1.	
Provide 3-point protection if cars are 
connected to locomotives and working on the 
ground when: 
	
• one or both feet enter between the rail, 
between equipment or within 15 feet of the 
end of the equipment; or 
	
• breaking the plane of the rail with your 
torso, between equipment or within 15 feet 
of the end of equipment. 
2.	
When applying 3-point protection the 
automatic brake is not required if the engineer 
ascertains that the locomotive brake(s) 
are sufficient to hold the equipment. The 
employee requesting the 3-point protection 
can still request that the automatic brake 
be applied if needed to prevent unintended 
movement. 
3.	
Any other department i.e. mechanical, 
engineering etc., that requests 3-point 
protection must have the automatic brake 
applied if applicable. 
4.	
When more than one employee requests 3-point protection, ensure that each 
employee cancels the requested protection before removing. 
Safe Work Procedure: Applying 3-Point Protection
Once a request for 3-point protection is received:
Step 1: 	
Apply engine brakes and automatic brake (if required) 
Step 2: 	
Center the reverser 
Step 3: 	
Open the generator field switch 
Step 4: 	
Communicate to your crew member that 3- point protection has 
been applied. 
Safe Work Procedure: Releasing 3-Point Protection
Once confirmation is received that 3-point protection is to be removed:
Step 1: 	
Close the generator field switch 
Step 2: 	
Move the reverser to forward or reverse 
Step 3: 	
Release the brakes 
Step 4: 	
Communicate to your crew member that 3-point protection has 
been released. 
23
White line indicates the plane 
of the rail.

Safe Work Procedure: Applying 3-Point Protection in Remote

Once a request for 3-point is received or 3-point is required: 
Step 1:

T-28 Avoiding Slips, Trips or Falls
To avoid slips, trips or falls, employees must: 
•	 Remain alert and mindful of your surroundings at all times; 
•	 Use designated walkways, crosswalks, handholds and railings when available; 
•	 Plan and choose routes that afford the safest walking conditions; 
•	 Keep a clear view of where you are walking; 
•	 Avoid carrying objects that block your view; 
•	 Keep locomotive cab, vehicle and other equipment floors clear of 
obstructions and tripping hazards; 
•	 For balance, keep hands out of pockets while walking. 
•	 When transporting an end of train (EOT) device, the device hoses must 
be secured.
